subject: Where should I look to restore geom_table behavior from ggExtra?

messages.author: afa289b81aad98c2
messages.subject: Where should I look to restore geom_table behavior from ggExtra?
parts:
I am *finally* getting around to updating a function that used to use
this code

p <- p + annotate("table", table[1], table[2], table = mod,
theme = theme.list(show.box = TRUE, separator = "black",
gp = gpar(cex = table[3]),
show.csep = TRUE, show.rsep = TRUE, show.colnames =
TRUE,
show.rownames = TRUE,
gpar.rowtext = gpar(col = "black", cex = 1.0, fontface
= "bold")))


which was based on ggExtra and put a nicely formated table on a plot.
When changes started to fly on ggplot2 and then ggExtra was
deprecated, there were some e-mails and suggestions about how to do a
table annotation in the new system. But, so much more has changed
since then. Can you guru's give me a suggestion about where to look
to begin restoring this functionality? Unless of course it is already
in there and I can't find it. This would be a single table in a
single panel; no faceting.

Thanks so much for not only this answer but all the work that's gone
into ggplot2 and friends lately. Bryan

messages.author: a3c668b849637905
messages.subject: Re: Where should I look to restore geom_table behavior from ggExtra?
parts:
Hi,

you can do it with ?annotation_custom ; you need to give it a grob,
e.g. from tableGrob(...).

I might post an example in the ggplot2 blog if no-one beats me to it
(please do).

HTH,

b.

messages.subject: Re: Where should I look to restore geom_table behavior from ggExtra?
parts:
Thanks Baptiste. Regarding annotation_custom, the help page example does this:

require(gridExtra)
base <- qplot(1:10, 1:10, geom = "blank") + theme_bw()
base + annotation_custom(grob = tableGrob(head(iris[ ,1:3])),
xmin = 3, xmax = 6, ymin = 2, ymax = 8)

But the position of the table on the resulting plot doesn't look right to me, or I misunderstand the documentation. The docs say that xmin etc is in data coordinates but the lower left hand corner of the table is not at 3,2 or even close. Can someone clarify?

Thanks, Bryan

messages.subject: Re: Where should I look to restore geom_table behavior from ggExtra?
parts:
On 7/12/2012 6:57 AM, Bryan Hanson wrote:
> Thanks Baptiste. Regarding annotation_custom, the help page example does this:
>
> require(gridExtra)
> base <- qplot(1:10, 1:10, geom = "blank") + theme_bw()
> base + annotation_custom(grob = tableGrob(head(iris[ ,1:3])),
> xmin = 3, xmax = 6, ymin = 2, ymax = 8)
>
> But the position of the table on the resulting plot doesn't look right to me, or I misunderstand the documentation. The docs say that xmin etc is in data coordinates but the lower left hand corner of the table is not at 3,2 or even close. Can someone clarify?

Yes, the Note in ?annotation_custom explains this. Essentially, the
table size is set by its content (otherwise cells would have a tendency
to be clipped or overlay each other, like in spreadsheets; because the
size of the grob is fixed, the positioning of the table only affects the
center of the table and it spreads on either side to its full size.
I have a prototype for a table where you can optionally set the width
manually, but it will be ready only after the gtable package is released.

HTH,

baptiste
